"DEADZONE — 3D ARENA FPS

Create a fully playable 3D first-person arena shooter called DEADZONE.

The game combines the tactical atmosphere of competitive military-style FPS games with the fast-paced arcade action of classic arena shooters.

Create an original game identity. Do not reproduce copyrighted characters, maps, weapon models, sounds, or assets from existing games.

1. VISUAL STYLE

- Fully 3D environment.
- First-person perspective.
- Dark futuristic industrial atmosphere.
- Detailed metallic corridors and combat arenas.
- Cinematic lighting and atmospheric fog.
- Realistic-stylized visual presentation.
- Explosions and visual effects.
- Smooth camera movement.

2. PLAYER CONTROLS

Implement:

- WASD movement.
- Mouse camera control.
- Sprint.
- Jump.
- Shooting.
- Reloading.
- Weapon switching.

For Android:

- Virtual joystick.
- Touch camera controls.
- Dedicated fire, reload, jump, and sprint buttons.

3. COMBAT SYSTEM

Implement several original fictional weapons with different gameplay characteristics:

- Standard energy rifle.
- Rapid-fire pulse weapon.
- Heavy fictional projectile launcher.

Each weapon should have:

- Unique visual design.
- Different firing behavior.
- Ammunition capacity.
- Reload animation.
- Distinct sound effects.

4. ENEMY AI

Create multiple fictional enemy types:

- Basic patrol units.
- Fast-moving arena enemies.
- Heavy armored enemies.

Enemies should have simple, readable game AI:

- Patrol designated areas.
- Detect the player within gameplay-defined ranges.
- React to player presence.
- Move around the arena.
- Engage using fictional projectile attacks.
- Have visible health indicators.

5. GAME MODES

Implement:

Arena Survival

- Survive successive enemy waves.
- Enemies become progressively more challenging.
- Display wave progression and score.

Target Practice

- Practice aiming and movement.
- Spawn stationary and moving targets.
- Track accuracy and score.

6. LEVEL DESIGN

Create one fully playable futuristic industrial arena.

Include:

- Multiple interconnected rooms.
- Open combat spaces.
- Elevated platforms.
- Cover objects.
- Atmospheric lighting.
- Distinct environmental details.

7. HUD AND UI

Display:

- Health.
- Armor.
- Ammunition.
- Current weapon.
- Wave number.
- Score.
- Minimap.

Create a polished futuristic interface.

8. AUDIO AND EFFECTS

Add:

- Original fictional weapon sounds.
- Environmental ambience.
- Footsteps.
- Reload sounds.
- Hit feedback.
- Explosions.
- Background music.

9. TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS

- Use Three.js or another suitable browser-compatible 3D engine.
- Implement actual 3D gameplay, not a 2D image pretending to be 3D.
- Ensure functional player movement and camera control.
- Implement collision detection.
- Optimize performance for Android.
- Include pause, restart, and settings menus.
- Prioritize a functional prototype over excessive visual complexity.

IMPORTANT: Build one polished, playable arena first. Do not attempt multiplayer networking yet.

Test player movement, camera controls, collision, shooting, enemy behavior, and mobile controls before completing the game.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable browser-based 3D first-person arena shooter called DEADZONE, prioritizing one polished arena and a functional prototype.

## Requirements
- Original dark futuristic industrial setting, first-person movement and combat, three fictional weapons, enemy types and AI, survival and target-practice modes, HUD/minimap, audio/effects, pause/restart, and Android touch controls.
- Use Three.js or another browser-compatible 3D engine; include collision, and test gameplay and mobile controls.
- No multiplayer or copyrighted game assets.

## Decisions
- Built a self-contained Three.js game in `index.html` using procedural geometry, synthesized audio, and original UI/weapon/enemy designs.
- Three.js is loaded from `https://unpkg.com/three@0.160.0/build/three.module.js`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the arena, first-person weapons, movement and collision, enemy behavior and attacks, wave survival and practice modes, HUD/minimap, audio effects, and touch controls in `index.html`.
- Verified the module parses with `node --check`.
- Started a local HTTP server and opened the game in Playwright; deployed from the menu and captured `screenshots/deadzone-check.jpg`.
- Fixed the CSS selector collision that made the HUD map canvas full-screen; `#map` now has dedicated styling.

### Active
- Validate the updated screenshot and test actual gameplay behavior, including controls, collision, shooting, enemy AI, wave progression, and mobile input.
- Inspect/fix any runtime issues and finalize the game.

### Blocked
- Browser check logged a favicon 404; not gameplay-blocking.
- No gameplay/mobile test results have been confirmed yet.

## Next Move
1. Read the latest `screenshots/deadzone-check.jpg` after the `#map` CSS fix (recapture first if needed).
2. Exercise survival and target-practice gameplay in Playwright; inspect the console and address issues.
3. Test mobile viewport/touch controls, then summarize assumptions and verification results.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Complete game implementation.
- `screenshots/deadzone-check.jpg`: Latest saved game screenshot; captured before the final map-canvas CSS fix.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Local server was started with `python3 -m http.server 3002`; URL is `http://localhost:3002`.
- Playwright browser is available after installing Chromium; `playwright-cli` is the test interface.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable browser-based 3D first-person arena shooter called DEADZONE, prioritizing one polished arena and a functional prototype.

## Requirements
- Original dark futuristic industrial setting, first-person movement and combat, three fictional weapons, enemy types and AI, survival and target-practice modes, HUD/minimap, audio/effects, pause/restart, and Android touch controls.
- Use Three.js or another browser-compatible 3D engine; include collision, and test gameplay and mobile controls.
- No multiplayer or copyrighted game assets.

## Decisions
- Built a self-contained Three.js game in `index.html` using procedural geometry, synthesized audio, and original UI, weapon, and enemy designs.
- Three.js is loaded from `https://unpkg.com/three@0.160.0/build/three.module.js`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the arena, weapons, movement and collision, enemy behavior and attacks, survival and practice modes, HUD/minimap, audio, and touch controls in `index.html`.
- Verified the extracted module parses using `node --check`.
- Opened the game in Playwright, deployed survival and practice modes, verified HUD/wave and enemy counts, pointer lock, weapon switching, and firing/ammo consumption.
- Confirmed the map canvas renders at the intended HUD size on desktop and mobile; tested mobile layout and touch-fire input.
- Captured `screenshots/deadzone-mobile.jpg`.

### Active
- Review the mobile screenshot and address any visible problems; if desired, continue testing mobile movement/look/reload/jump/sprint.
- Consider a favicon to clear the browser’s non-gameplay 404.

### Blocked
- No known blockers.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `screenshots/deadzone-mobile.jpg` for layout issues.
2. Further verify touch movement/look and the remaining touch controls if useful.
3. Summarize results and note any remaining polish needs.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Complete game implementation.
- `screenshots/deadzone-mobile.jpg`: Latest mobile gameplay capture.
- `screenshots/deadzone-check.jpg`: Earlier desktop capture, taken before the map canvas CSS fix.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Local server is available at `http://localhost:3002`.
- Browser console showed only a favicon 404 and SwiftShader/WebGL performance warnings; no gameplay JavaScript errors observed.
